ApiKeyCreated.description:
The one shape that carries the secret, returned by exactly one
endpoint, exactly once. The key is not stored, so this response is the
only opportunity anyone will ever have to read it -- which is why the
management UI (T-313) shows it with an unmissable warning and holds it in
component state rather than in the react-query cache.
ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated

ApiKeyUpdateRequest.description:
PATCH semantics: every field optional, and the service writes only the
keys the caller actually sent (`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`).

Scopes are deliberately absent. Widening a live key's scopes is the same
act as minting a new key with more access, minus the audit trail and
minus the chance to rotate the secret -- so it is not an edit, it is a
new key and a revocation.
ApiKeyUpdateRequest.title: ApiKeyUpdateRequest

GlobalBannerResponse.description:
T-263's `global_banner` setting, rendered above the app shell on web
and mobile. Absent (null) whenever no banner is set.
GlobalBannerResponse.title: GlobalBannerResponse

InvitationPublic.description:
One pending invitation, as the org's own admins see it.

Field-by-field rather than from_attributes over the whole Invitation row
on purpose: that row carries `token_hash`, and the accept URL's security
rests on the token being unguessable. An explicit allowlist means a
future column added to the model can't ride out to the client the way
`model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` plus a wildcard would
(§0.4). `expires_at` is here so the caller can render an unaccepted-but-
expired invite as expired rather than as still-live.
InvitationPublic.title: InvitationPublic

MaintenanceResponse.description:
T-263. Reported here -- on the one endpoint the maintenance middleware
deliberately never blocks -- so a client that is being 503'd everywhere
else can still learn *why*, and render the operator's copy instead of a
generic network error.
MaintenanceResponse.title: MaintenanceResponse

SsoHintResponse.description:
What the login page needs to replace a password field with a button.

`sso_available: false` is the answer for every domain with no *opt-in*
connection -- including domains that have one with hinting turned off.
The two are deliberately indistinguishable from outside: that is the
whole point of the flag.
SsoHintResponse.title: SsoHintResponse

WebhookEndpointCreated.description: The one shape that carries a new endpoint's signing secret.
WebhookEndpointCreated.title: WebhookEndpointCreated

WebhookEndpointUpdateRequest.description:
PATCH semantics: every field optional, and the service writes only the
keys the caller actually sent.

`event_types` *is* editable here, unlike `ApiKey.scopes` -- and the
difference is not an inconsistency. Widening a key's scopes silently gives
an existing credential more power; subscribing an endpoint to another
event only sends it more of the product's own data, to a URL its owner
already proved they control.
WebhookEndpointUpdateRequest.title: WebhookEndpointUpdateRequest

WebhookEventTypePublic.description:
One entry of the event catalogue the UI's multi-select renders from
(T-322) -- derived from app.modules.webhooks.events, never a second
hardcoded list.
WebhookEventTypePublic.title: WebhookEventTypePublic

WebhookSecretRotated.description:
The rotation response: the new secret, and the moment the old one stops
being accepted. Both matter -- a rotation whose overlap window a consumer
cannot see is a rotation they have to guess the deadline for.
WebhookSecretRotated.title: WebhookSecretRotated

post.description: Creates an API key and returns it **once**. The key is not stored and cannot be retrieved again; every later read returns the prefix only. Valid scopes: orgs:read, members:read, members:write, files:read.

Revokes a key immediately. The row stays visible with `revoked_at` set, so an incident review can still see what the key could reach. Idempotent: revoking an already-revoked key is a 200 and does not move the timestamp.

schema.title: Response Login Api V1 Auth Login Post

put.description: Creates or replaces this organization's identity provider. The discovery document is fetched and its `issuer` compared against the one supplied before anything is written, so the most common misconfiguration fails here rather than for every member at once at the next sign-in.

post.description: Whether an email domain signs in with SSO. Answers `false` for every domain whose organization has not opted in, so this endpoint cannot be used to discover which domains have accounts here.

get.description:
Send the browser to the organization's IdP.

The always-available entry point: it works whether or not the
organization opted into domain hinting, which is what makes hinting a
convenience rather than a requirement.
The organization record. Callable with an API key holding the `orgs:read` scope, or with a session belonging to the organization.
The organization's members, cursor-paginated. Callable with an API key holding the `members:read` scope, or with a session belonging to the organization.

post.description: Sends the stored payload again as a **new** delivery, with a new `X-Forge-Delivery` id. The original row is never modified -- the log is an audit trail, so 'we replayed it and now it says delivered' is a sentence this API cannot produce.

Registers an endpoint and returns its signing secret **once**. The secret is stored encrypted and is never returned by any later read; rotate it if it is lost. The URL is checked against the outbound guard both here and again immediately before every delivery.

get.description: One endpoint's delivery log, newest first, paginated by keyset (`after` carries the previous page's last id). Payloads are omitted here and returned by the single-delivery read.

post.description: Issues a new signing secret and returns it once. The previous secret keeps working for 24 hours -- every request in that window is signed with both, so a consumer can deploy a verifier that accepts either and switch over without downtime.

get.description: Every event this product can emit, with a one-line description. Rendered by the management UI's event picker and by the published documentation, so a newly registered event appears in both without a second list to update.

schema.title: Response Health Live Health Live Get
